summary: Every course must be letter graded when the instructor offers a letter grade, and a course counts toward one requirement only, except that the WIM course (CEE 100 or 102W) also counts elsewhere. You pick one of the four subplans, and the audit checks its 36 units of math and science (one math sequence, not mixed, and one chemistry option), Technology in Society, Engineering Fundamentals, 40 units of depth with two Focus Breadth Electives, and the CEE 183 capstone, for 93 units in all; Urban students also take CEE 100. Your advisor checks the 2.0 GPA in fundamentals and depth courses, and honors adds a 3.3 GPA, an approved proposal and the thesis. Left: Energy's chemistry rule lists both CHEM 31A and CHEM 31E as required with no text to say otherwise, and the Electives section asks Coastal students for one breadth elective where the subplan asks for two; the subplan's two is used.
